newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy sugar beet sowings seen higher in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Italy sugar beet sowings seen higher in 1996/97.

text.p: Italy's spring sugar beet sowings should total 225,638 to 234,937 hectares, concentrated in northern and central parts of the country, the Italian Sugar Beet Producers Association said.
Total Italian sugar sowings for this year's campaign, including some earlier sowings in southern Italy, should total 270,638 to 279,937 ha, up from 247,699 last year.

Total plantings, under normal weather conditions, should allow Italy to produce 1.5-1.6 million tonnes of sugar, of which 1.26-1.30 million would be in northern and central Italy. In the last crop season Italy produced 1.435 million tonnes of sugar, of which 1.21 million was in northern and central Italy.
Italy's Sugar Association said this would be enough to cover the European Union quota for Italy and domestic consumption needs.

In 1996 farmers switched out of sugar beet and planted more maize and soy because prices were much higher than average. In 1997 the situation has reversed, according to the Sugar Association, which represents 90 percent of sugar producers here.
